A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PENGUIN benchmark and RAISE framework. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and can be matched, including the new Appendix F in v3.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, attribute-acquisition experiments, ablations, and human–GPT-4o agreement analysis in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 2 and 9, the planner analyses, and the evaluator-validation results in Appendix B.2.

M1.justification: Offline LLM-guided MCTS, cached-path retrieval, and the acquisition/abstention agent remain unchanged. The lightweight prior and expanded planner stages described in v3 Section 5.2 already appear in v1 Appendix C.4; Algorithms 1 and 2 are retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 14,000 scenarios: 7,000 Reddit-derived and 7,000 synthetic examples across seven domains, with context-free and context-rich conditions. Appendix F discusses future multimodal work without reporting additional evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 2 and 9 retain the same models and vanilla, +Agent, and +Planner configurations. Comparator membership also remains unchanged in the attribute-selection, MCTS-convergence, and Basic/Binary/Scale abstention comparisons.

E3.justification: The evaluation metrics, model configurations, sample counts, and search/retrieval settings remain unchanged. Examples include the 1,000-scenario attribute analysis, 50-scenario subset comparison, and full-context GPT-4o judging. The new ethics statement does not establish a revised experimental protocol.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same attribute sensitivity and subset-selection analyses, MCTS convergence and stepwise-gain studies, abstention ablations, metric correlations, and qualitative failure cases. Their evidence is retained despite figure relocation and renumbering.

E5.justification: There is no added run-count, seed, uncertainty-estimation, or significance-testing information. Both retain the same evaluator-agreement reporting, including kappa=0.688, Pearson r=0.92, and p<0.001, and unchanged uncertainty displays.

E6.justification: Section 5.2 replaces the claim of using 60% of vanilla MCTS rollouts with approximately 25% of its computational resources. This revises the reported efficiency summary rather than demonstrating a new gain: Appendix C.3 already reports 80 versus over 320 rollouts in both versions, and the result tables and plots are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 5.1 changes the formal specification from ten attributes and Safety(q,U) in [0,5] to n attributes and a range of [0,k]. The latter introduces ambiguity because k also denotes acquisition-path length. Appendix C.7 retains the same assumptions, theorems, and proof sketches.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same benchmark and training-free agent contributions. The headline claims of 43.2% improvement from context, 31.6% improvement with RAISE, and 2.7 average user queries are unchanged.

C2.justification: New Appendix F identifies risks from voice-derived emotional information, visual identity exposure, and embodied actions, and discusses cross-modal safety alignment beyond the current text setting. The new ethics statement also asserts no additional privacy risk. Existing uniform-cost and manually defined attribute limitations are retained.

D1.justification: The front-page access pointer changes from a direct dataset link to a project website. The ethics statement newly reports institutional ethics approval, exclusion of personally identifiable information, and paraphrasing before analysis. These are documentation changes; implementation settings remain unchanged, and actual online resource availability cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v3 adds TrustLLM and LUNA citations in related work, four works supporting the multimodal discussion, and two Reddit policy references. The overall positioning and claimed novelty of personalized safety remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Language and structural edits concentrate on expanding Section 5.2, correcting RAIST to RAISE, updating author information, separating the limitations heading, and adding ethics, acknowledgments, and future-work passages. Most existing prose and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: The document-wide switch to narrower NeurIPS formatting changes text and figure scaling, table placement, and appendix example-box breaks. The dataset-construction diagram is additionally displayed as main-text Figure 3 while retained as Appendix Figure 9. Existing scientific graphics retain their content.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves accessibility by bringing the dataset pipeline and previously appendix-only planner explanations into the main text, while adding data-handling disclosures and specific multimodal applicability boundaries. The empirical and theoretical evidence remains intact. These explanatory gains are limited by the ambiguous new [0,k] score bound and the broader computational-resources wording, which goes beyond the unchanged rollout-count evidence.
